title: Keeping a Conversation Going with Follow-up Questions
meta: B2 · 约 280 词 · 场景：用追问延续闲聊

sections.heading: 1. Jumping Versus Digging
paragraphs: Picture this exchange at the coffee machine.
"I went hiking last weekend," says your colleague.
"Oh, nice," you reply, and then you ==abruptly== ask about the project deadline.
Nothing went wrong, exactly, but the conversation just died.
Your colleague ==volunteered== a topic, and you jumped away from it.
**Most conversations do not end because people run out of things to say; they end because nobody digs.**
Digging means staying with the same topic for two or three more questions.
It can feel ==intrusive== at first, but most people enjoy talking about something they chose to __bring up__ themselves.
You are not being nosy; you are giving them permission to keep going.
A good rule is to ask at least two follow-ups before you change the subject.
paragraphs_zh: 想象一下咖啡机旁的这段对话。
「我上周末去徒步了。」同事说。
「哦，不错。」你回了一句，然后突然问起项目 deadline。
说起来也没出什么错，但天就这么聊死了。
同事主动抛了个话题，你却跳开了。
大多数对话结束，不是因为没话可说；而是因为没人往下挖。
深挖的意思是，在同一个话题上再多问两三个问题。
一开始可能会觉得有点冒犯，但大多数人都喜欢聊自己主动提起的事。
你不是在八卦；你是在给对方接着往下讲的许可。
一个好用的规矩是：换话题之前，至少追问两句。

sections.heading: 2. Three Follow-ups That Always Work
paragraphs: The first is the detail question: "Where did you go?" or "How long was the trail?"
It is easy to answer and shows you are __tuned in__.
Keep it light, though, and do not turn the chat into an interview.
The second is the experience question: "What was the best part?" or "Was it as hard as you expected?"
This invites a short story, and stories are where people __open up__.
The third is the future question: "Would you do it again?" or "Where's next on your list?"
It shows ==curiosity== about the person, not just the event, and it often ==reveals== what they really enjoy.
Between questions, ==echo== a word or two from their answer.
If they say, "The view at the top was unreal," you can say, "Unreal? Better than the photos?"
**Echoing a single word is the easiest follow-up in English, and it buys you time to think.**
paragraphs_zh: 第一种是细节题：「去的哪儿？」或者「那条路线有多长？」
好回答，也说明你在认真听。
不过要轻松点，别把闲聊变成面试。
第二种是体验题：「最棒的是哪一段？」或者「跟你预想的一样累吗？」
这会引出一个小故事，而人往往是在讲故事的时候才打开话匣子。
第三种是未来题：「还会再去吗？」或者「下一个想去哪儿？」
这说明你好奇的是这个人，而不只是这件事，而且往往能看出他真正喜欢什么。
问题和问题之间，重复一两个对方回答里的词。
如果他说：「山顶的风景简直不真实。」你可以接：「不真实？比照片还好看？」
重复一个词，是英语里最省力的追问，还能给你争取点思考时间。

gist.q: 作者说大多数对话为什么会冷掉？
gist.a: 不是没话可说，而是没人往下“挖”：对方抛出话题，我们却跳到别的事上。

gist.q: 三种万能追问分别是什么？
gist.a: 细节问题（去哪了、多远）；经历问题（最好的部分是什么、比预想难吗）；未来问题（还会再去吗、下一站去哪）。

gist.q: echo 技巧是什么？有什么好处？
gist.a: 重复对方回答里的一两个词并加问号接着问；这是最简单的追问，还能给自己争取思考时间。

prompts.q: 印度同事说他上周末回家参加了朋友的婚礼。用细节、经历、未来三种追问，加上 echo，把对话聊 30 秒。
prompts.ref: Oh, a wedding! Was it back home in India? Three days? Wow. What was the best part, the food or the dancing? Ha, I believe it. I've never been to an Indian wedding. Would you say it was a typical one, or bigger than usual? Next time a friend of yours gets married, I want a full report.
prompts.ref_zh: 哦，婚礼！是回印度老家吗？三天？哇。最棒的是哪部分，吃的还是跳舞？哈，我信。我还没参加过印度婚礼。你觉得这算是典型的规模，还是比一般的更大？下次你朋友结婚，我要听完整汇报。

prompts.q: 会前同事随口说 I've started learning to cook. 用 echo 和追问聊 30 秒。
prompts.ref: Learning to cook? That's great. What made you start? Delivery fatigue, I get that. What's the first dish you managed to get right? Pasta from scratch? That's ambitious. Was it as hard as you expected? I tried making dumplings once and they all fell apart in the pot, so I'm genuinely impressed. What's next on your list?
prompts.ref_zh: 在学做饭？挺好的。怎么想起来学的？外卖吃腻了，懂。第一道做成功的菜是什么？手擀意面？够有野心的。跟你想的一样难吗？我有次试着包饺子，下锅全散了，所以我是真心佩服。下一道打算做什么？

words.ex: The call ended abruptly when his connection dropped.
She volunteered to take notes, which helped a lot.
Asking about salary in the first chat can feel intrusive.
Good managers show curiosity about how their people like to work.
The user interviews revealed a problem we had never seen in the data.
I echoed her last point to show I'd understood it.
If the numbers look odd, dig a bit before you report them.
Ask a quick question now and then to show you're tuned in.
He only opened up about the burnout in our third one-on-one.
